ocr.notes: Mostly right, but the first challenge reads '$1,000 to $5,000' (OCR '$3,000'), and the stakes in Allen's quote are dollars, not pounds ('$1,000 to $5,000'). 'Pittsburg', 'begged of McCoole's seconds' and 'proved' in the image.

title.suggested: The Pugs - Allen and Mace Bantering Each Other for Another Bruising Match

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Republican reprinted a New York Times item in which Tom Allen answered Jem Mace, offering to fight him under the new London prize ring rules for $1,000 to $5,000 a side in Kansas, New Orleans or Canada.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads 'The St. Louis Republican, Saturday Morning, February 28, 1874', page 5. Item is a New York dispatch dated Feb. 26 quoting the next day's New York Times.

facts.fact: Allen issued a challenge to fight Jem Mace, Joe Coburn or any man in the world for $1,000 to $5,000
Mace, then in London, sent word that he would return to America and fight Allen on Allen's terms

Allen offered to fight Mace under the new London prize ring rules for $1,000 to $5,000 a side in Kansas, New Orleans or Canada, and to meet Mace's backers at Pittsburg or Cincinnati to sign articles with a $500 deposit
Allen offered as alternatives to fight Joe Coburn, wagering $2,500 to $1,500, or Ben Hogan for $1,000 to $5,000

facts.quote: I am surprised that Jem Mace thinks I do not mean business. He knows that I never backed out. ... I mean business, and hope Mace, Coburn and Hogan will not refuse to meet me.

facts.fact: The paper recalled that Mace defeated Allen in New Orleans in May 1870, and that Allen's last fight, against McCoole on Chouteau Island, Illinois, was in the fall of 1873

notes: Current title has 'The Bugs'; the head reads 'THE PUGS'. The paper says Mace would be backed from New York and Allen from St. Louis.
